root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening, widening, or becoming unclosed, whether as a physical gap or as release from constraint.
root_idea.development: From physical opening and intervening space, the lexicon develops meanings for fissures, access points, bodily openings, relief from grief, exposure, and related derived states. Some specialized usages depart from this central pattern, notably the technical term مُفْرَجٌ for an unallied or unidentified slain person.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form فَرَجَ; the Quran occurrence is its passive feminine form.
Displayed as the nominal citation form فَرْجٌ, covering its Quranic singular and plural inflections.

senses.definition: To open, cleave, or split apart; in the Quranic occurrence, to be opened or cleft.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the passive perfect feminine form فُرِجَتْ, describing the sky becoming opened, cloven, or rent.

senses.definition: A fissure, rift, cleft, or opening.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural فُرُوجٍ, specifically used of cracks or rifts in the structure of the sky.

senses.definition: The pudendum; by euphemistic extension, chastity or sexual modesty.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with singular and plural possessive forms for the sexual private parts, and in contexts of guarding or preserving chastity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an opening or intervening space between two things; to open a thing, door, or mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active Form I construction describes causing an interstice or opening, including opening a door or opening the mouth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make room or provide space for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people making ample space for a person in a place of standing or sitting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove, clear away, or dispel grief or sorrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used with عَنْ in the construction فَرَجَ اللهُ عَنْهُ غَمَّهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have the pudendum habitually uncovered while sitting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A state or behavior described of a person whose private parts remain exposed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have buttocks that do not meet, or scarcely meet, because of their size.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an additional bodily description in the lexical entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become extremely old, aged, or weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clear away from someone or something, leave its way, or abandon a place; to disperse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people removing themselves from a road or place, and of dust becoming dispersed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's shooting or casting to deteriorate after having been good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage referring to a change for the worse in marksmanship or casting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a she-camel to become loosened in the hip joints during a difficult first parturition, and thereby distressed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized childbirth construction, also yielding the sense distressed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divert, amuse, or cheer oneself; to seek entertainment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often followed by عَلَى and an object viewed for diversion; the entry characterizes this use as possibly postclassical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open, gape, become unclosed, or become loosened and unknotted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a physical opening, a bone, limb, or joint; of a bow, its curved extremities may stand apart from the string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break off from or interrupt speaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported construction meaning to desist from speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For grief, sorrow, or anxiety to be removed, cleared away, or dispelled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intransitively of distress coming to an end.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become happy or cheerful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived Form VII emotional-state usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of having the pudendum habitually uncovered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive or quasi-verbal-noun use describing persistent exposure while sitting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relief from grief, sorrow, anxiety, difficulty, distress, or constraint; ease after trouble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of release or clearing away, as in expressions for the removal of grief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the dish جُوذَابَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiomatic name rather than a productive general meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose pudendum is habitually uncovered while sitting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of the person exhibiting the condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of diversion or amusement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a place in which تفَرُّج, diversion or pleasing pastime, is found.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The space between the hind legs, or between the fore and hind legs, of a horse or similar animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Extended idiomatically to expressions for a horse running at full speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The external sexual organs or pudendum of a person or animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical usage can include male, female, and juvenile humans and animals; common parlance often specifies the anterior pudendum, while legal usage may include both anterior and posterior parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An open tract, entrance, pass, or frontier route; especially an exposed place of danger requiring protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the opening of a valley or road, a mountain pass, and a vulnerable access route into a country.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow whose limbs stand wide apart from the string.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term describes the open space between the bow's curved extremities and its string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman wearing a single garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal usage attributed to Yemen, with a corresponding Najdi form reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who does not conceal a secret, or who habitually reveals secrets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival characterization of indiscretion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of defeat or rout.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in the expression for overtaking a group while they were in defeat; an alternative reading of the expression is also transmitted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opening, gap, or intervening space between things, including a gap in a wall or room made among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of unoccupied spaces in rows or ranks, such as gaps in a prayer row.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female animal or woman whose joints have become loosened through parturition; by extension, a fatigued camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a ewe or woman after giving birth and of a she-camel fatigued as compared with that condition; it can also denote a she-camel bearing her first offspring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uncovered, exposed, appearing, or apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a correction of a variant explanation and applied, for example, to a pearl exposed for sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who frequently removes or dispels grief or anxiety from afflicted people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young domestic hen or chicken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Has the plural فَرَارِيجُ and a reported dialectal variant with initial dammah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slit-backed cloak or garment, or a child's shirt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The garment is named for its opening or slit; the usage is also attested for a fur-lined or silk garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose hip joints have become loosened through parturition and which consequently dislikes the stallion's approach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal description related to the postpartum sense of فَرِيجٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having teeth with spaces between them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression أَفْرَجُ الثَّنَايَا, synonymous with أَفْلَجُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having buttocks that do not meet, or scarcely meet, because of their size.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is فَرْجَاءُ; the description is reported especially among Abyssinians.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who beats, washes, and whitens clothes; a fuller or laundry worker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational noun synonymous with قَصَّارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opening or slit, especially an interstice between fingers, an aperture in a railing, or a slit in a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural forms تَفَارِيجُ are used for these openings and garment slits.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cowardly and weak; one who becomes defeated or flees in battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Several forms with or without initial ن are reported for this adjectival usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of opening, outlet, or egress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes an opening of the mouth and places through which one exits.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person without an alliance, kin, or supporting relations; in a legal usage, an unidentified slain person or an unallied dependent for whom compensation is borne by the community or treasury.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry records variant explanations and a disputed distinction from مُفْرَحٌ; the definition here represents the reported ج reading and its associated legal-social senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose shooting or casting has deteriorated after previously being good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hen that has chicks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine-less adjectival or nominal animal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel whose elbows are distant from the armpits, giving it a wide stance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form applies to a she-camel with wide armpits because of the elbow position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A comb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal usage recorded without further qualification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opened door.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial nominal use.

cautions: The Quranic plural فُرُوجٍ in 50:6 denotes fissures or rifts in the sky, while the other Quranic occurrences of فَرْجٌ and فُرُوجٌ use the anatomical or euphemistic chastity sense.

The Lane discussion of the technical term مُفْرَجٌ records variant readings and several attributed explanations; the classical entry preserves that reported lexical branch without treating the variants as separate Quranic forms.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:frj:33639:g3:sub4 reports an additional sense of فَرِجَ as being liberated from cares or joyful, but explicitly states that its authority could not be found; it is therefore left unassigned rather than presented as established evidence.
